title: Unpinned Third-Party Dependencies
damaged_code:
```toml
# Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
# Unpinned dependency pulls breaking build reproducibility
tokio = "1" 
```
pattern: Declaring external crate dependencies using wide, unpinned version ranges or omitting exact semantic locks.
why_bad: Ensures that build behavior is non-deterministic over time. A compile run today might work, while another tomorrow will fail or compile insecure code because an upstream library published a broken version.
detection: A project that lacks a version lockfile (e.g., `Cargo.lock` in Rust, `package-lock.json` in Node) checked into its repository, or using `*` version markers.
counterexample:
```toml
[dependencies]
tokio = "=1.28.0" # Lock explicitly, backed by Cargo.lock
```
fix: Pin exact minor and patch versions under version control; commit the package manager's generated lockfile to guarantee consistent, reproducible build runs.
source: Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright - *Software Engineering at Google_ Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 16 / Chapter 21.
